title: Liquid Glass — your synthesis
question: Your steer, built. One world across the three surfaces you specified: canon arrangement as the default, the Register discipline as map mode, the fold sequence on vehicle detail with real photography. The buff/paper palette is gone — this is bright, modern liquid glass. All three cards lock the same world; they exist so you can see every surface. Re-roll if it still is not right.

options.label: Default mode
options.lineage: Apple Liquid Glass, canon marketplace arrangement
options.thesis: The familiar three-column arrangement, executed in glass at a craft level the category does not reach.
options.viewport: Glass nav bar full width with the search capsule inside it. Filter rail left, result rows centre with real scooter photography and ₹ totals, live terrain map right. One row selected in amber.
options.risk: The familiar arrangement only earns its keep if the glass and type are genuinely better than the category's — at anything less it just looks like everyone else.

raised.raise: Canon arrangement becomes the default mode rather than an alternative world.
Every stacked offer is enumerated with its own values — depth never implies a count.
Selection and focus carried by luminance, not hue — what lets an amber pin survive green terrain.
A date or filter change shows its consequence before it commits.

options.label: Map mode
options.lineage: Apple Liquid Glass over live terrain; the Register's stamped-record discipline
options.thesis: When you want every shop at once, the terrain becomes the whole page and the glass floats on it.
options.viewport: Terrain edge to edge. A glass shop list on the left with distance, rating and ₹ price per row, the selected row lifted in amber. Floating search capsule above.
options.risk: Pins must read against both snow and forest — in the build they get a white halo and a luminance step, not just amber fill.

options.label: Vehicle detail
options.lineage: Apple Liquid Glass; the Fold Sequence's visible-step discipline
options.thesis: Real photography of the actual scooter, and a booking sequence where every completed step stays visible.
options.viewport: Large scooter photograph with thumbnails left. Glass stack right: total, refundable deposit, cancellation terms, spec strip, amber book action. A slim numbered step column down the right edge, current step marked by one amber dot.
options.risk: The step column turns into a progress bar in costume unless earlier steps stay genuinely readable.
